Key Activities: Leads and coordinates the 7-day statistical data collection activities for either telephone interviewing (CATI) or personal interviewing (CAPI or PAPI) programs; including the management of the Statistical Survey Operations (SSO) Interviewers and Senior Interviewers as well as the supervision of subordinates and interdisciplinary teams.
Assesses the cost, quality, efficiency, productivity and security of the functions and activities associated with the data collection, processing, editing, and compilation of statistical outputs.
Evaluates trends and developments in data collection concepts, methods and techniques including response patterns and respondent behaviour.
Participates in the development of strategies and business solutions for data collection and transmission requirements.
Sollicits participation from non-respondents and resolves complaints.
Acts as a regional representative on departmental projects, task forces and committees and provides advice on proposed questionnaire design and survey content and coverage.

1. Decision making: Prepares and reviews correspondence, manuals and data to ensure completeness, accuracy, integrity and compliance with job requirements. Develops and implements alternate work methods and models and proposes changes and improvements to questionnaire design, enhancements or modifications to survey content and coverage, revisions to collection systems and processes, and the implementation of new hardware and software for use in data collection activities.
Develops operational plans and schedules to manage, organize and control the 7-day data collection activities.

Develops guidelines, instructions and procedures for the use and evaluation of statistical systems and processes and for the maintenance and safeguarding of computer systems, equipment, databases and files.

Identifies and assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and the associated costs and limitations to identify the availability of respondents and to ensure quality control of data, to evaluate the suitability of new hardware and software, and to identify and determine the short and long term program impact and benefits.
2. Leadership and operational management: Leads and coordinates multi-disciplinary project teams, committees or work groups comprising professional, technical, administrative and interviewers engaged in initiating, developing and implementing programs. Identifies and recommends human resources needs and levels to meet program and project goals and objectives within branch mandate. Approves work plans and priorities. In collaboration with Regional Management, establishes organizational structures, recommends classification levels, assigns responsibilities to team or group members, monitors progress and performance, provides guidance and direction on career development and approves individual training plans.
Establishes and monitors program budgets, including both main estimate and cost recovery funding, to ensure that funds are spent appropriately, with authority to reallocate funds among line objects.

Plans and budgets for the management and operation of the regional CATI or CAPI program in accordance with departmental policy and procedures. Responsibilities include identifying content and cost of development and operational requirements, estimating salary and travel costs, professional fees and equipment costs.
3. Communication: Discusses and negotiates with subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and other stakeholders to come to an agreement on the development of questionnaires, collection applications, and the framework and conditions within which statistical programs will occur. There is a requirement to understand issues and to resolve differences that can affect the efficiency and quality of program operations and outputs.
Responds orally or in writing to inquiries from managers, employees and the general public to provide information and advice, to solicit participation from non-respondents and to resolve complaints.

Prepares schedules, work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources involved in the operation of statistical collection systems and processes. The information is used by senior management to prepare program plans and has an impact on the nature, scope and cost of divisional statistical activities.

Prepares evaluation reports outlining the effectiveness of existing and new statistical systems and processes and the quality and completeness of data. Senior management uses this information to assess the attainment of program objectives and the cost, efficiency and utilization of regional resources.

Provides advice to senior management and subject matter experts regarding proposed changes to questionnaire design, modifications to survey content and coverage, revisions to collection systems and processes, and the implementation of new hardware and software used in data collection activities.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Practical knowledge of socio-economic concepts, methods and techniques applied in the development and operation of statistical programs.

Knowledge of financial and human resources management, and of project management methods, techniques and practices to develop proposals and work plans, to establish and monitor resource requirements, schedules and progress, to establish and manage project teams, and to resolve problems related to the development and operation of the division's systems and processes.
Knowledge of questionnaire development to outline specifications and requirements for the collection and processing of statistical information and to provide feedback to subject matter experts.
Knowledge of communication principles and techniques in order to negotiate program requirements, present and explain options and recommendations and resolve operational disputes.
Knowledge of training methods, techniques and practices to develop and present operational training modules.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of trends and developments in data collection processes to select and integrate new computer hardware and software technology and applications in mass statistical data capture and conversion systems and processes.
Knowledge of the trends and developments in data collection concepts, methods and techniques to evaluate response patterns and respondent behavior and to provide feedback to subject matter experts.

Knowledge and understanding of Statistics Canada’s mandate, programs, objectives, policies and procedures in areas such as survey methodology, operations integration, data confidentiality and security, dissemination and marketing to coordinate and ensure the development and operation of divisional programs consistent with departmental requirements.

Knowledge of the content and operation of the Agency’s household and business survey programs and their impact upon systems and processes to determine and devise procedures and standards to be applied in operational activities.
Knowledge of the Statistical Survey Operations organization, its collective agreements, grievance procedures, policies and directives to ensure equitable treatment of all staff.
Knowledge of the Regional Operations Branch mandate, objectives, standards and procedures to coordinate and manage on-going development and operational activities and/or special projects.
Knowledge of the structure and operation of internal client organizations to establish and maintain a framework for the collection, exchange and dissemination of information.

Knowledge and understanding of the structure, operation and practices of Statistics Canada and Regional Operations Branch service areas, such as human resources and finance, in order to access the services of such areas.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act pertaining to data security and confidentiality to ensure adherence in all development and operational activities. Knowledge of the Canada Labor Code to ensure safe working conditions exist for all employees. Knowledge of the Financial Administration Act, the Public Service Employment Act and related policies and directives.
6. Research and analysis: Evaluates trends and developments in data collection concepts, methods and techniques, including response patterns and respondent behaviour. Prepares assessments of questionnaire design, concepts, change in technology, respondent reaction and understanding for feedback to senior management and survey clients.

Interprets the relative quality of data produced, determines reasons for variances, its comparability over time and its relevancy in light of changing requirements, trends, developments, policy issues and socio-economic conditions.

Reviews and modifies existing operational techniques, methods and approaches or develops new ones to meet specific needs. Operational programs may involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses).

Reviews and resolves gaps and inconsistencies in the collection methods and procedures, reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs, reviews and resolves technical and conceptual problems referred by staff or project teams. Analysis is required to understand and interpret client requirements and to translate them into a concrete, timely and affordable information request. Clients are often uncertain of their data needs and are unfamiliar with statistical options, methods and techniques available.

Job Poster.Assets: Essential qualifications Bilingual Imperative (CBC/CBC). EDUCATION: Successful completion of two years of post secondary education with acceptable specialization in social science, statistics, library/archival work or law related field, or acceptable combination of education, training and/or experience. EXPERIENCE: Recent and significant experience managing survey collection in a production environment geared toward results and respondent relations; Recent experience establishing collaborative working relationships; Recent experience performing operational planning in a data collection environment; Recent and significant experience supervising employees doing data collection; Experience managing and forecasting expenses. ABILITIES: Ability to analyze and evaluate resources required for data collection programs; Ability to coordinate multiple simultaneous and interrelated activities; Ability to manage statistical survey projects. COMPETENCIES: Thinking things through; Demonstrating integrity and respect; Working effectively with others. PERSONAL SUITABILITIES: Leadership; Judgement.
Job Poster.Area of Selection: Employees of Statistics Canada occupying a position in the Montreal region.
